fact: Arcep announced on 16 February 2024 the launch of phase 2 of the Universal Service of electronic communications, funded by a telecom-operator fund, to extend coverage to 200 villages in all nine provinces.
Arcep says phase 1 of the Universal Service (2016-2018) installed 18 radio stations benefiting 33 villages on the Makokou-Okondja and Okondja-Aboumi roads.
Minister Marc Alexandre Doumba said the government intends to accelerate deployment of the universal service to open up rural zones and improve connectivity in the interior.

Digital economy minister Mark Alexandre Doumba said his ministry is working with ARCEP, under the amending finance law, on a programme for connectivity of public infrastructure in rural areas (schools, community centres, multimedia rooms, hospitals), to start from May 2026.
system: Programme dedicated to connectivity of public infrastructure in rural zones

fact: ARCEP's board chairman Celestin Kadjidja says that, of 20 universal-service sites planned for rural connectivity, three have been built and are to be commissioned within days.
Minister Mark-Alexandre Doumba said more than 200 villages are still not connected to the internet and that a Universal Service Fund (Fonds du service universel) is being set up to give them access.
